Role in the communication stack: signals at the top, I-PDUs at the bottom

AUTOSAR COM connects the signal-oriented view of the RTE with the PDU-oriented lower layers. Upwards, COM provides transmit and receive services for individual signals, signals of dynamic length, and signal groups, such as Com_SendSignal, Com_ReceiveSignal, Com_SendSignalGroup, and Com_ReceiveSignalGroup ([SWS_Com_00197], [SWS_Com_00198], [SWS_Com_00200], [SWS_Com_00201], [SWS_Com_00627]). Downwards, the PDU Router is the only partner. COM transmits via PduR_ComTransmit ([SWS_Com_00669]). Conversely, the PduR calls Com_RxIndication, Com_TxConfirmation, Com_TriggerTransmit, and the TP functions of COM (SWS PduR p. 24).

The BswM controls COM from the side. It starts and stops I-PDU groups, switches receive deadline monitoring, and selects the transmission mode (SWS BswM p. 93). COM reports development and runtime errors to the DET ([SWS_Com_00670]). The supported data types are boolean, unsigned and signed integers up to 64 bits, float32/float64, and uint8[n]. The latter is mapped to UINT8_N or UINT8_DYN ([SWS_Com_00675]), and such signals must be byte-aligned ([SWS_Com_00105]).

Context diagram: COM is located between RTE and PduR, is controlled by the BswM, and reports errors to the DET. Sources: SWS PduR p. 24, SWS BswM p. 93, [SWS_Com_00669], [SWS_Com_00670]

Lifecycle: Com_Init, I-PDU groups, and Com_DeInit

Com_Init initializes the internal and external interfaces. However, communication between ECUs remains blocked afterwards ([SWS_Com_00432]). An exception is made for I-PDUs that are not assigned to any group. Com_Init starts them itself, as if Com_IpduGroupStart had been called with initialize = true ([SWS_Com_00840]). Their initial transmission mode results from the ComSignalInitValues ([SWS_Com_00877]). Com_GetStatus provides the module state COM_UNINIT/COM_INIT ([SWS_Com_00194], [SWS_Com_00819]).

An I-PDU is active as soon as at least one of its groups is started ([SWS_Com_00771]). All I-PDUs of a group have the same ComIPduDirection ([SWS_Com_00871]).

  • Com_IpduGroupStart starts a group. With initialize = true, its I-PDU data is reinitialized ([SWS_Com_91001]). In the BswM, this corresponds to the parameter BswMPduGroupSwitchReinit (SWS BswM p. 165).
  • The first cyclic transmission after starting the group follows after the timeOffset of the CyclicTiming (SystemTemplate p. 268).
  • Com_IpduGroupStop cancels pending transmit requests of the affected I-PDUs, including retries ([SWS_Com_91002], [SWS_Com_00777]). COM ignores transmit confirmations arriving afterwards ([SWS_Com_00800]).
  • Com_DeInit stops all started groups and sets COM to the uninitialized state ([SWS_Com_00130]).

State diagram: Lifecycle of an I-PDU between module initialization, group start/stop, and deinitialization. Sources: [SWS_Com_00432], [SWS_Com_00840], [SWS_Com_00771], [SWS_Com_91001], [SWS_Com_91002], [SWS_Com_00130]

Transmission: from signal value to confirmed I-PDU

For atomic data, the RTE writes each group signal individually with Com_SendSignal. It then triggers the transmission with Com_SendSignalGroup (SWS RTE p. 329). In doing so, COM sets the update bit of the group ([SWS_Com_00801]). The transmit services operate asynchronously. They return E_OK or COM_SERVICE_NOT_AVAILABLE if the associated I-PDU group is stopped ([SWS_Com_00197], [SWS_Com_00865]).

What the functions called by the RTE do not handle directly is taken over by Com_MainFunctionTx ([SWS_Com_00399]). Before I-PDU processing, it calls Com_CbkTxPrep if required ([SWS_Com_00886], [SWS_Com_91013]). If a configured Com_TxIpduCallout returns false, the I-PDU is not processed further ([SWS_Com_00346]). If retries are configured, the minimum delay only starts if PduR_ComTransmit returns E_OK ([SWS_Com_00828]). Com_TxConfirmation reports success or failure ([SWS_Com_00124]), and each successful transmission triggers the configured notification ([SWS_Com_00883], [SWS_Com_00468]).

Sequence diagram: A signal group is filled, transmitted via PduR and CanIf, and confirmed. Sources: SWS RTE p. 329, SWS PduR p. 33, [SWS_Com_00399], [SWS_Com_00124]

For trigger-transmit bus interfaces such as FlexRay, the interface initially only remembers the transmission request. It requests the data later via the PduR with Com_TriggerTransmit (SWS PduR p. 106, [SWS_Com_00001]). In two cases, COM does not copy anything and returns E_NOT_OK: if the buffer is too small or the I-PDU is stopped ([SWS_Com_00869], [SWS_Com_00884]).

Sequence diagram: With Trigger Transmit, the transmission request and data retrieval are decoupled in time. Sources: SWS PduR p. 106, [SWS_Com_00001], [SWS_Com_00869], [SWS_Com_00884]

The transmission time can be influenced externally in three ways:

  • Com_SwitchIpduTxMode sets the transmission mode. Cyclic transmissions are shifted by ComTxModeTimeOffset in the process ([SWS_Com_00784], [SWS_Com_00881], SWS BswM p. 178).
  • Com_TriggerIPDUSend triggers a single transmission, regardless of the transmission mode. This is effective only if the I-PDU is started ([SWS_Com_00348], [SWS_Com_00861], SystemTemplate p. 371).
  • Com_TriggerIPDUSendWithMetaData works similarly, but passes metadata that applies only to this single transmission ([SWS_Com_00858], [SWS_Com_00862], [SWS_Com_00887]). The J1939Rm uses this variant (SWS J1939Rm p. 62).

Reception: check chain and consistent signal groups

The PduR passes received I-PDUs with Com_RxIndication ([SWS_Com_00123], SWS PduR p. 103). COM then runs through a check chain:

  1. A configured Rx callout receives the complete I-PDU. It is always called, specifically before counter handling ([SWS_Com_00816], [SWS_Com_00889]). If it returns false, the I-PDU is not processed ([SWS_Com_00700]).
  2. If the I-PDU counter differs, COM calls Com_CbkCounterErr ([SWS_Com_00726]).
  3. If the update bit is not set, the signal is discarded ([SWS_Com_00802]). If the update bit is missing because the I-PDU is too short, the signal is considered updated ([SWS_Com_00794]).
  4. If COM filters out a group signal, it discards the entire signal group ([SWS_Com_00836]).

Activity diagram: Branches during reception of an I-PDU up to the notification. Interpretation: The sequence of update bit before filter is shown, but not verified. Sources: [SWS_Com_00889], [SWS_Com_00700], [SWS_Com_00802], [SWS_Com_00794], [SWS_Com_00836], [SWS_Com_00555]

On the receive side, the RTE calls Com_ReceiveSignalGroup exactly once and then reads the group signals with Com_ReceiveSignal. COM only notifies once all signals of the group are unpacked into a buffer (SWS RTE p. 329, [SWS_Com_00201]). COM stores received metadata for access via Com_ReceiveSignalWithMetaData ([SWS_Com_00888], [SWS_Com_91005]).

Array access, large I-PDUs, and transformers

Com_SendSignalGroupArray and Com_ReceiveSignalGroupArray transport a signal group as a uint8 array. The array extends from the start byte of the group signal with the smallest to the last byte of the group signal with the highest ComBitPosition ([SWS_Com_00851], [SWS_Com_00854], [SWS_Com_00844], [SWS_Com_00845]). Conditions apply to this access:

  • The group contains only fixed-size data, is byte-aligned, and does not enclose any foreign signals ([SWS_Com_00841]).
  • For such a group, the individual signal and normal group APIs are not available ([SWS_Com_00843]).
  • The APIs must be enabled via ComEnableSignalGroupArrayApi ([SWS_Com_00853], [SWS_Com_00856]).

For transmission mode selection, COM treats array transmission like Com_SendSignalGroup ([SWS_Com_00847]). The COM Based Transformer uses precisely this path (SWS ComXf p. 14).

Large I-PDUs run via the TP interface. For reception, these are Com_StartOfReception, Com_CopyRxData, and Com_TpRxIndication ([SWS_Com_00691], [SWS_Com_00692], [SWS_Com_00650]). With TpSduLength = 0, COM reports back the configured maximum length ([SWS_Com_00874]). For transmission, these are Com_CopyTxData and Com_TpTxConfirmation ([SWS_Com_00693], [SWS_Com_00725], SWS SecOC p. 108). If another transmit request arrives during an ongoing transmission, COM skips it ([SWS_Com_00863]). In contrast, a Com_TriggerIPDUSend with a locked buffer is stored and performed later ([SWS_Com_00867]).

Sequence diagram: Segmented reception of a large I-PDU via CanTp and PduR up to the result evaluation. Sources: SWS SecOC p. 111, [SWS_Com_00691], [SWS_Com_00692], [SWS_Com_00650], [SWS_Com_00838]

Main functions, time monitoring, and signal gateway

COM has three cyclic main functions: Com_MainFunctionRx, Com_MainFunctionTx, and Com_MainFunctionRouteSignals ([SWS_Com_00398], [SWS_Com_00399], [SWS_Com_00400]). Their periods are described by the time bases comConfigurationRxTimeBase, comConfigurationTxTimeBase, and comConfigurationGwTimeBase (SWC-Template p. 841). If there are multiple instances of a main function, ComIPduMainFunctionRef assigns each I-PDU to one of them (SWS RTE p. 1470).

Transmit deadline monitoring works as follows:

  • The timer starts upon transmission, provided it is not already running. For the first start after a (re)start of monitoring, ComFirstTimeout applies, otherwise ComTimeout ([SWS_Com_00878], [SWS_Com_00879]).
  • A transmit confirmation stops the timers ([SWS_Com_00880]).
  • If a timer expires, COM calls the ComTimeoutNotifications ([SWS_Com_00304]).
  • In transmission mode NONE, monitoring is disabled ([SWS_Com_00835]).

Upon reception, a timeout can replace the values with ComTimeoutSubstitutionValue ([SWS_Com_00875], [SWS_Com_00876]). This monitoring can be enabled and disabled per group ([SWS_Com_91003], [SWS_Com_91004]).

Activity diagram: Start, cancellation, and expiration of transmit deadline monitoring. Sources: [SWS_Com_00835], [SWS_Com_00878], [SWS_Com_00879], [SWS_Com_00880], [SWS_Com_00304]

The signal gateway is an integral part of COM (SRS Gateway p. 11). It can route group signals to individual signals ([SWS_Com_00833]) and undergoes defined processing stages on the receive and transmit sides ([SWS_Com_00872], [SWS_Com_00873]).

Behavior in the event of an error

  • COM reports development errors to Det_ReportError with ModuleId 50 ([SWS_Com_00442]). The error codes are:
    • COM_E_PARAM ([SWS_Com_00803])
    • COM_E_UNINIT for API calls before Com_Init or after Com_DeInit, except for status, version, and main functions ([SWS_Com_00804])
    • COM_E_PARAM_POINTER ([SWS_Com_00805])
    • COM_E_INIT_FAILED ([SWS_Com_00837])
  • A skipped transmit request of a large I-PDU is reported as runtime error COM_E_SKIPPED_TRANSMISSION ([SWS_Com_00863], [SWS_Com_00864]).
  • When a group is stopped, the services return COM_SERVICE_NOT_AVAILABLE. If the buffer of a large I-PDU is locked, COM_BUSY may be returned ([SWS_Com_00865]). Com_CbkTxErr indicates a transmission attempt with a stopped group ([SWS_Com_00491]).
  • A TP reception with E_NOT_OK or a callout result false causes COM to treat all signals of the I-PDU as invalidated and execute the ComDataInvalidActions ([SWS_Com_00838], [SWS_Com_00839]).
  • On the sender side, Com_InvalidateSignal and Com_InvalidateSignalGroup invalidate values ([SWS_Com_00203], [SWS_Com_00557]). On the receiver side, a configured invalid value also requires a ComDataInvalidAction ([SWS_Com_00859], [SWS_Com_00860]). The reception of invalid values is reported via Com_CbkInv ([SWS_Com_00536]).
  • Com_ReceiveSignalGroupArray returns the last known data or initial values even when the I-PDU is stopped ([SWS_Com_00857]).

Further detailed evidence

  • API core and status types: [SWS_Com_00432], [SWS_Com_00130], [SWS_Com_00825] (implementation-specific Com_ConfigType), [SWS_Com_00820]/[SWS_Com_00822] (identifier types).
  • Symbolic names of the ComSignal handles are generated from the configuration (ECU Configuration p. 138).
  • SWS PduR p. 33 shows the interaction between PduR and handle IDs on the transmission and confirmation path.
  • Control by the BswM is described by SWS BswM p. 148 (deadline monitoring) and SWS BswM p. 165 (groups).
  • For array access and transformers: [SWS_Com_00846], [SWS_Com_00848], [SWS_Com_00850], and Layered SW Architecture p. 103.
  • SRS RTE p. 41 covers the cyclic scheduling of Com_MainFunctionTx by the RTE. SWS RTE p. 832 describes the callback Rte_COMCbkTxPrep.

function Com_Init [SWS_Com_00432] 📄 PDF

void Com_Init (const Com_ConfigType* config);

This service initializes internal and external interfaces and variables of the AUTO- SAR COM module layer for the further processing. After calling this function the inter - ECU communication is still disabled. In configurations, in which Com is assigned to mo re than one partition (i.e. Com_ Main Functions are mapped to partitions), Com may provide one init function per AUTOSAR CP R20 - of Document ID : AUTOSAR_SWS_COM partition.

function Init [SWS_Com_00130] 📄 PDF

void Com_De Init (void);

This service stops the inter - ECU communication. All started I - PDU groups are stop- ped and have to be started again, if needed, after Com_ Init is called. By a call to Com_ De Init the AUTOSAR COM module is put into an not initialized state.

function Com_IpduGroupStart [SWS_Com_91001] 📄 PDF

void Com_IpduGroupStart (Com_IpduGroupIdType Ipdu GroupId, boolean initialize);

Starts a preconfigured I - PDU group. For example, cyclic I - PDUs will be sent out cyclically after the call of Com_ Ipdu Group Start(). If Initialize is true all I - PDUs of the I - PDU group shall be (r e - )initialized before the I - PDU group is started. That is they shall behave like after a start - up of COM, for example the old_ value of the filter ob- jects and shadow buffers of signal groups have to be (re - )initialized.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: f964dc667e23 Provenance

use

The synchronous function [SWS_Com_91001] starts a pre-configured I-PDU group. After the call, cyclic I-PDUs of this group, for example, are sent cyclically. The interface has no return value (void) and is provided via the header Com.h (service ID 0x03).

The function expects two input parameters:

  • IpduGroupId (type Com_IpduGroupIdType): Identifies the ID of the I-PDU group to be started.
  • initialize (type boolean): Controls whether the data of the I-PDUs of this group shall be initialized or re-initialized before the start.

If initialize is passed with true, all I-PDUs of the group behave as after a start-up of the COM module. This means that, among other things, the values of old_value for filter objects as well as the shadow buffers of signal groups are (re-)initialized before the start of the I-PDU group.

Concurrency and Limitations

Regarding concurrency behavior, Com_IpduGroupStart is reentrant for different I-PDU groups. For the same I-PDU group, the function is non-reentrant; competing or nested calls with an identical IpduGroupId are therefore not permitted.

function Com_IpduGroupStop [SWS_Com_91002] 📄 PDF

void Com_IpduGroupStop (Com_IpduGroupIdType Ipdu GroupId);

Stops a preconfigured I - PDU group. For example, cyclic I - PDUs will be stopped after the call of Com_ Ipdu Group Stop().

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 3cd410e4c939 Provenance

The function Com_IpduGroupStop ([SWS_Com_91002]) serves to deactivate or stop a pre-configured I-PDU group in the communication module Com. After the service is called, the associated communication processes are stopped; for example, cyclic I-PDUs are stopped after calling Com_IpduGroupStop ([SWS_Com_91002]).

Call and Parameters

The function is provided via the header Com.h and has the service ID 0x04. Execution is synchronous, and the function returns no value (void).

  • IpduGroupId (input parameter of type Com_IpduGroupIdType): Identifier (ID) of the pre-configured I-PDU group to be stopped ([SWS_Com_91002]). Input/output parameters (inout/out) are not present for this call.

Concurrency and Reentrancy

The function Com_IpduGroupStop is reentrant for different I-PDU groups, but non-reentrant for the same I-PDU group ([SWS_Com_91002]). For parallel calls from different contexts for the same group ID, it must therefore be ensured that no concurrent execution takes place.

This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification AUTOSAR Classic R20-11.

function Com_EnableReceptionDM [SWS_Com_91004] 📄 PDF

void Com_EnableReceptionDM (Com_IpduGroupIdType Ipdu GroupId);

Enables the reception deadline monitoring for the I - PDUs within the given I - PDU group.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: c68cd88180d9 Provenance

use

The function Com_EnableReceptionDM ([SWS_Com_91004]) activates the reception deadline monitoring (Reception Deadline Monitoring) for all I-PDUs assigned to the passed I-PDU group. The call is processed synchronously and has the service ID 0x06. The interface is provided via the header Com.h.

  • Parameters: Via the input parameter IpduGroupId (type Com_IpduGroupIdType), the identifier of that I-PDU group is passed for whose I-PDUs deadline monitoring is to be activated.
  • Return value: The function returns no value (void) and has no input/output or output parameters.

Concurrency and Limitations

With regard to concurrency behavior, Com_EnableReceptionDM according to [SWS_Com_91004] is reentrant for different I-PDU groups. However, for the same I-PDU group, the function is non-reentrant (Non reentrant for the same I - PDU group). Usage and Semantics

The function Com_ReceiveDynSignal ([SWS_Com_00690]) represents a synchronous service that copies payload data of a signal with dynamic length. The desired signal is addressed via parameter SignalId. The received data is copied to the memory location pointed to by SignalDataPtr, while the actual signal length is returned via Length ([SWS_Com_00690]).

The parameter Length functions as an in/out parameter: Upon the call, it must specify the maximum receivable buffer size as input. After successful processing, it contains the actual length of the received dynamic signal as output ([SWS_Com_00690]). The interface is available via header Com.h.

Error Handling and Return Values

The execution status is signaled via the return value of type uint8 ([SWS_Com_00690]):

  • E_OK: The service was successfully accepted and the data was copied.
  • E_NOT_OK: The value of Length passed as input is smaller than the actual length of the received dynamic signal.
  • COM_SERVICE_NOT_AVAILABLE: The associated I-PDU group was stopped or the service failed due to a development error.
  • COM_BUSY: The associated transport protocol buffer (TP buffer) is locked.

Concurrency and Limitations

Com_ReceiveDynSignal is reentrant for different signals, but not reentrant for the same signal ([SWS_Com_00690]). Concurrent calls for the same SignalId must therefore be avoided by appropriate protection mechanisms at the caller level.

The synchronous function Com_ReceiveSignalGroupArray copies the received signal group array representation from the I-PDU into the memory area referenced by the output parameter SignalGroupArrayPtr ([SWS_Com_00854], [SWS_Com_00855], [SWS_Com_00849]). Interpretation: Prior to triggering the copy operation into the I-PDU, the individual group signals in the shadow buffer are likely to have been fully updated in order to ensure data consistency within the group.

Interaction

The service joins the signal and PDU processing functions of module Com. It extends the regular transmission of individual signals via Com_SendSignal ([SWS_Com_00197]) or the invalidation of signal groups via Com_InvalidateSignalGroup ([SWS_Com_00557]) by directly providing metadata. In addition, other metadata-capable services exist in the module, such as PDU-based Com_TriggerIPDUSendWithMetaData ([SWS_Com_00858]) on the transmit side or Com_ReceiveSignalWithMetaData ([SWS_Com_91005]) on the receive side.

This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR specification R20-11.

The synchronous function Com_TriggerIPDUSend ([SWS_Com_00348]) is used for the targeted triggering of the transmission of an I-PDU based on the input parameter PduId. The interface is provided via the header Com.h.

Error Handling and Return Values

The function returns as return value of type Std_ReturnType ([SWS_Com_00348]):

  • E_OK: Transmission of the I-PDU was successfully initiated.
  • E_NOT_OK: The I-PDU is in the stopped state; transmission could not be initiated.

According to [SWS_Com_00861], AUTOSAR COM initiates the transmission of the affected I-PDU only if the I-PDU is started.

Interaction with Large I-PDUs

If a large I-PDU (Large I-PDU) is triggered via Com_TriggerIPDUSend and its buffer is currently locked, AUTOSAR COM does not discard the transmit request. Instead, the transmit request is buffered and the I-PDU is automatically transmitted as soon as the buffer is released again ([SWS_Com_00867]).

Concurrency and Limitations

The function is specified as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) ([SWS_Com_00348]). Therefore, calls with identical contexts must not occur concurrently or preemptively without appropriate synchronization.

function Com_TriggerTransmit [SWS_Com_00001] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Com_TriggerTransmit (PduIdType TxPduId, PduInfoType* PduInfoPtr);

Within this API , the upper layer module (called module) shall check whether the available data fits into the buffer size reported by Pdu Info Ptr - >Sdu Length. If it fits, it shall copy its data into the buffer provided by Pdu Info Ptr - >Sdu Data Ptr and update the length of the actual copied data in Pdu Info Ptr - >Sdu Length. If not, it returns E_ NOT_ OK without changing Pdu Info Ptr.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: d75bf7e2399d Provenance

use

The function Com_TriggerTransmit is called synchronously to query and provide SDU data for an upcoming transmission [SWS_Com_00001]. The SDU to be transmitted is identified via the input parameter TxPduId [SWS_Com_00001]. Via the in-out parameter PduInfoPtr, the caller provides a pointer to the destination buffer (SduDataPtr) as well as the buffer size available there (SduLength) [SWS_Com_00001].

Within the call, the module checks whether the available data fits completely into the provided buffer [SWS_Com_00001]:

  • If the buffer is sufficient, the module copies the data into the destination buffer SduDataPtr, updates PduInfoPtr->SduLength with the actual number of copied bytes, and returns E_OK [SWS_Com_00001].
  • If the SduLength specified in the passed buffer is smaller than the actual PDU length, Com_TriggerTransmit copies no data at all, does not modify PduInfoPtr, and returns E_NOT_OK [SWS_Com_00001] [SWS_Com_00869].

Error handling

An abort with the error value E_NOT_OK also occurs if the requested I-PDU is stopped; in this case as well, no data is copied [SWS_Com_00884]. If the service returns E_NOT_OK, the caller must not under any circumstances use PduInfoPtr, as it may contain a NULL pointer or point to invalid data [SWS_Com_00001].

Concurrency and Limitations

The function is reentrant for different PDU IDs, but must not be called reentrantly for the same PDU ID [SWS_Com_00001]. The declaration is available via header Com.h [SWS_Com_00001].

This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification AUTOSAR CP R20-11.

function Com_StartReception [SWS_Com_00691] 📄 PDF

BufReq_ReturnType Com_Start Of Reception (PduIdType id, const PduInfoType* info, , PduLengthType* buffer SizePtr);

Service Com_StartReception.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 81596d76f6c3 Provenance

The synchronous and reentrant function Com_StartReception ([SWS_Com_00691]) is called at the start of the reception of an N-SDU. This comprises both segmented transmissions (First Frame with subsequent Consecutive Frames) and unsegmented individual frames (Single Frame). The declaration is available via Com.h.

Parameters and Call Semantics

  • id: Identification of the I-PDU to be received.
  • info: Pointer to an PduInfoType structure containing payload data as well as metadata of the first or individual frame. If neither payload nor metadata is present, this parameter must be set to NULL_PTR.
  • TpSduLength: Total length of the N-SDU to be received. If the service is called with an TpSduLength of 0, it returns the currently maximum available buffer size.
  • bufferSizePtr: Output parameter for the buffer available in the receiving module. This value serves the calling transport protocol module for calculating the Block Size (BS).

Return Values and Error Handling

The result of the buffer request is signaled via the return type BufReq_ReturnType:

  • BUFREQ_OK: The connection is accepted and reception continues. bufferSizePtr contains the size of the available buffer. If no buffer of the requested size can be provided, the value 0 is returned via bufferSizePtr.
  • BUFREQ_E_NOT_OK: The connection is rejected and the reception process is aborted. The value of bufferSizePtr remains unchanged.
  • BUFREQ_E_OVFL: No buffer of the required length can be allocated; reception aborts and bufferSizePtr remains unchanged.

This usage note was generated by an AI based on the specification state of AUTOSAR CP R20-11.

The function Com_CopyRxData ([SWS_Com_00692]) is called synchronously to provide received data of an I-PDU segment (N-PDU) to the upper layer. For segmented transmissions, each call delivers the respective next part of the I-PDU data. The identification of the received I-PDU is performed via the parameter id.

The source buffer (SduDataPtr) and the number of bytes to be copied (SduLength) are passed via the parameter info. A value of 0 for SduLength can specifically be used to query the currently available buffer size of the upper layer; in this scenario, SduDataPtr may be passed as NULL_PTR ([SWS_Com_00692]). Via the output parameter bufferSizePtr, the function reports the buffer size remaining after the copying process.

The following requirements apply to execution and error handling ([SWS_Com_00692]):

  • Concurrency: The function is specified as reentrant.
  • Return values: BUFREQ_OK confirms the successful copying of the data. If an error occurs, BUFREQ_E_NOT_OK is returned and the data is not copied.

function Com_CopyTxData [SWS_Com_00693] 📄 PDF

BufReq_ReturnType Com_CopyTxData (PduIdType id, const PduInfoType* info, const RetryInfoType* retry, PduLengthType* available DataPtr);

Service Com_CopyTxData.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 516aabd6462f Provenance

use

The synchronous interface Com_CopyTxData ([SWS_Com_00693]) is called by lower-layer modules (such as transport protocols) to query transmit data for segments (N-PDUs) of an I-PDU. Each call sequentially provides the next data segment, provided no retransmission is requested.

  • id: Identifies the I-PDU to be transmitted.
  • info: Points to the buffer structure (PduInfoType). SduDataPtr receives the data, SduLength determines the requested byte count. A value of 0 for SduLength can be used to signal state changes via retry or to query remaining data; in this case, SduDataPtr may be a NULL_PTR.
  • retry: Controls confirmation and error recovery. If the pointer is NULL_PTR, copied data may be removed from the buffer immediately after copying. If it points to a structure (RetryInfoType), TpDataState determines the behavior:
    • TP_CONFPENDING: Previously copied data must remain in the TP buffer for error recovery.
    • TP_DATACONF: Confirms all data copied prior to this call so that it may be deleted (excluding data of the current call).
    • TP_DATARETRY: Instructs the function to copy data again starting from the offset TxTpDataCnt (relative to the current copy position).
  • availableDataPtr: Writes the number of bytes remaining in the Tx buffer as an output parameter, which enables TP modules with dynamic payload length to determine the size of subsequent segments.

Return Values and Error Handling

The result of the request is reported via BufReq_ReturnType:

  • BUFREQ_OK: Data was completely copied into the buffer as requested.
  • BUFREQ_E_BUSY: Data could not be provided because the required amount is not yet available in the upper module. No data was copied; the lower-layer module may repeat the call later.
  • BUFREQ_E_NOT_OK: The request failed; no data was copied.

Concurrency

According to the specification, the function is defined as reentrant ([SWS_Com_00693]).

This usage note is based on the AUTOSAR CP R20-11 specification.

Implementer's Guide to follow (complexity I1)

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: cd82ba3d0afe Provenance

Usage and Call Context

The callback function Com_CbkCounterErr ([SWS_Com_00726]) serves to signal incorrect I-PDU counter values. It is called immediately by the AUTOSAR COM module as soon as an incoming I-PDU has a counter value that deviates from the expected value.

The call is performed synchronously (Synchronous) and returns no value (void). The following context information is transmitted via the input parameters:

  • ComPduId (PduIdType): The identifier of the I-PDU in which the counter error was detected.
  • ExpectedCounter (uint8): The counter value expected by the COM module.
  • ReceivedCounter (uint8): The counter value transmitted in the received I-PDU.

Concurrency and Error Handling

For reentrancy, don't care is specified ([SWS_Com_00726]). Since the function is called immediately upon detection of the deviation, the actual execution context (e.g. task or interrupt context) is likely to depend on the configuration of the higher-level reception processing.

The provision of the callback interface is configurable (Available via configurable). Specific error codes, standardized DET/DEM messages, or return values for error handling are not defined in [SWS_Com_00726].

function Com_RxIpduCallout [SWS_Com_00700] 📄 PDF

boolean Com_RxIpduCallout (PduIdType PduId, const PduInfoType* PduInfoPtr);

The I - PDU callout on receiver side can be configured to implement user - defined receive filtering mechanisms.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 96ea8f894cf9 Provenance

The function Com_RxIpduCallout ([SWS_Com_00700]) serves as a configurable callout on the receiver side to implement user-specific filter mechanisms for incoming I-PDUs.

Usage and Semantics

The call to Com_RxIpduCallout is performed synchronously with service ID 0x2A ([SWS_Com_00700]). The function has two input parameters:

  • PduId: Identifier of the received I-PDU ([SWS_Com_00700]).
  • PduInfoPtr: Pointer to a structure of type PduInfoType, which provides the length (SduLength) of the received I-PDU as well as a pointer to its payload (SduDataPtr) ([SWS_Com_00700]).

According to [SWS_Com_00816], the AUTOSAR COM module forwards the complete data of the received I-PDU, as passed by the PDU Router (PduR), to Com_RxIpduCallout.

Return Values and Filtering

Via the return value of type boolean, the processing flow in the COM module is controlled ([SWS_Com_00700]):

  • true: The received I-PDU is processed normally.
  • false: The I-PDU is discarded and not processed further.

Concurrency and Error Handling

Regarding reentrancy, the function is classified with the property don't care ([SWS_Com_00700]). Specific return codes for errors or notifications to DET or DEM are not defined for this interface in the specification.

This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR specification R20-11.

function Com_TxIpduCallout [SWS_Com_00346] 📄 PDF

boolean Com_TxIpduCallout (PduIdType PduId, PduInfoType* PduInfoPtr);

The I - PDU callout on sender side can be configured for example to implement user - defined transmission filtering or user - defined pre - transmission - processing of the outgoing I - PDU.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 8a216e409b62 Provenance

use

The configurable callout function Com_TxIpduCallout ([SWS_Com_00346]) is called on the sender side to perform user-defined transmission filtering (user-defined transmission filtering) or user-defined pre-transmission processing (user-defined pre-transmission-processing) before transmitting an outgoing I-PDU.

The call is synchronous (Synchronous) under service ID 0x29. For reentrancy, don't care is specified.

Parameters and Return Value

  • PduId (in): Designates the identifier of the transmitted I-PDU (ID of the transmitted I-PDU).
  • PduInfoPtr (inout): Pointer to structure PduInfoType. It contains the length (SduLength) of the sent I-PDU as well as a pointer to its payload data (SduDataPtr).

Via the boolean return value, the callout decides on the further course of action:

  • true: The I-PDU is processed further normally (I-PDU will be processed normal).
  • false: The I-PDU is discarded and not processed further (I-PDU will not be processed any further).

Error Handling and Concurrency

No DET or DEM error messages are defined in the specification element for Com_TxIpduCallout. Since reentrancy is declared as don't care, the specification places no specific requirements on the reentrancy of the implementation.

type Com_StatusType [SWS_Com_00819] 📄 PDF

This is a status value returned by the API service Com_ Get Status().

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 6f7752d0bee1 Provenance

According to [SWS_Com_00819], the enumeration type Com_StatusType describes the initialization and operating state of the AUTOSAR COM module. The type is declared via the header file Com.h and serves as the return value of the API service Com_GetStatus().

Value Range and Semantics

  • COM_UNINIT: Has the fixed numerical value 0x00 (value 0). This state signals that the AUTOSAR COM module is not initialized or not usable. According to [SWS_Com_00819], this is mandatorily the default value immediately after a reset.
  • COM_INIT: Indicates that the AUTOSAR COM module has been successfully initialized and is operational or usable.

use

As the return type of the function Com_GetStatus(), Com_StatusType serves to determine the operational readiness of the module. The COM module is only usable after switching to the state COM_INIT, whereas no regular use is possible under COM_UNINIT [SWS_Com_00819].

Specific error codes, DET or DEM messages, as well as specifications regarding reentrancy or concurrency are not defined for this type in the specification, as it is an elementary status enumeration.

This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification of AUTOSAR R20-11.

Initialization and status

Com_DeInit function

This service stops the inter - ECU communication. All started I - PDU groups are stop- ped and have to be started again, if needed, after Com_ Init is called. By a call to Com_ De Init the AUTOSAR COM module is put into an not initialized state.

void Com_De Init (void);
Com_GetStatus function

Returns the status of the AUTOSAR COM module. Availab le via Com.h

Com_StatusType Com_GetStatus (void);
Com_GetVersionInfo function

Returns the version information of this module.

void Com_GetVersionInfo (Std_VersionInfoType* versioninfo);
Com_Init function

This service initializes internal and external interfaces and variables of the AUTO- SAR COM module layer for the further processing. After calling this function the inter - ECU communication is still disabled. In configurations, in which Com is assigned to mo re than one partition (i.e. Com_ Main Functions are mapped to partitions), Com may provide one init function per AUTOSAR CP R20 - of Document ID : AUTOSAR_SWS_COM partition.

void Com_Init (const Com_ConfigType* config);

Com_IpduGroupStart function

Starts a preconfigured I - PDU group. For example, cyclic I - PDUs will be sent out cyclically after the call of Com_ Ipdu Group Start(). If Initialize is true all I - PDUs of the I - PDU group shall be (r e - )initialized before the I - PDU group is started. That is they shall behave like after a start - up of COM, for example the old_ value of the filter ob- jects and shadow buffers of signal groups have to be (re - )initialized.

The service Com_ Switch Ipdu Tx Mode sets the transmi ssion mode of the I - PDU refe- renced by Pdu Id to Mode. In case the requested transmission mode was already active for this I - PDU, the call will have no effect.

By a call to Com_ Trigger IPDUSend With Meta Data the AUTOSAR COM module updates its internal metadata for the I - PDU with the given ID by copying the metada- ta from the given position and with respect to length of the globally configured Meta Data Type of this I - PDU. Then the I - PDU is triggered for transmission.

  <p>The function <code>Com_TriggerTransmit</code> is called synchronously to query and provide SDU data for an upcoming transmission <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00001" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00001">[SWS_Com_00001]</a>. The SDU to be transmitted is identified via the input parameter <code>TxPduId</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00001" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00001">[SWS_Com_00001]</a>. Via the in-out parameter <code>PduInfoPtr</code>, the caller provides a pointer to the destination buffer (<code>SduDataPtr</code>) as well as the buffer size available there (<code>SduLength</code>) <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00001" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00001">[SWS_Com_00001]</a>.</p>
  <p>Within the call, the module checks whether the available data fits completely into the provided buffer <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00001" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00001">[SWS_Com_00001]</a>:</p>
  <ul>
    <li>If the buffer is sufficient, the module copies the data into the destination buffer <code>SduDataPtr</code>, updates <code>PduInfoPtr-&gt;SduLength</code> with the actual number of copied bytes, and returns <code>E_OK</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00001" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00001">[SWS_Com_00001]</a>.</li>
    <li>If the <code>SduLength</code> specified in the passed buffer is smaller than the actual PDU length, <code>Com_TriggerTransmit</code> copies no data at all, does not modify <code>PduInfoPtr</code>, and returns <code>E_NOT_OK</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00001" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00001">[SWS_Com_00001]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00869" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00869">[SWS_Com_00869]</a>.</li>
  </ul>
  <h4>Error handling</h4>
  <p>An abort with the error value <code>E_NOT_OK</code> also occurs if the requested I-PDU is stopped; in this case as well, no data is copied <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00884" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00884">[SWS_Com_00884]</a>. If the service returns <code>E_NOT_OK</code>, the caller must not under any circumstances use <code>PduInfoPtr</code>, as it may contain a NULL pointer or point to invalid data <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00001" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00001">[SWS_Com_00001]</a>.</p>
  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>The function is reentrant for different PDU IDs, but must not be called reentrantly for the same PDU ID <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00001" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00001">[SWS_Com_00001]</a>. The declaration is available via header <code>Com.h</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00001" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00001">[SWS_Com_00001]</a>.</p>
  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification AUTOSAR CP R20-11.</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="782e9d7551f78bb718e09a472888188cfe02e7e0692c9deda73a46cbc6f87568" data-trace-output="e800ab77905411a6d571730122ed892f3835af384453b5298b57eac3e9dd06b6" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>use</h4>
  <p>The function <code>Com_RxIndication</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00123" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00123">[SWS_Com_00123]</a>) is used to indicate a received PDU from a lower layer communication interface module (<em>lower layer communication interface module</em>) to the COM module. The declaration is available via the header file <code>Com.h</code>. The service has the Service ID <code>0x42</code>, is executed synchronously, and has no return value (<code>void</code>).</p>
  <p>The interface expects two parameters:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>RxPduId</code>: Identifier (ID) of the received PDU (of type <code>PduIdType</code>).</li>
    <li><code>PduInfoPtr</code>: Pointer to a structure of type <code>PduInfoType</code>. This contains the length of the received PDU (<code>SduLength</code>), a pointer to the buffer with the PDU data (<code>SduDataPtr</code>), and the associated metadata.</li>
  </ul>
  <p>Neither input/output parameters nor output parameters are specified.</p>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00123" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00123">[SWS_Com_00123]</a>, the function is reentrant for different PDU IDs (<code>Reentrant for different Pdu Ids</code>). For the same PDU ID, however, execution is non-reentrant (<code>Non reentrant for the same Pdu Id</code>). Lower-layer modules must therefore not call <code>Com_RxIndication</code> concurrently or pre-emptively for an identical <code>RxPduId</code>.</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note is based on the AUTOSAR specification R20-11 and was created automatically.</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="8076e4116d3d547cdd24351821d7f7bdbdb972d5d0b0c41bdd6ec6a2e315e079" data-trace-output="1138495e4d4170a72cee7fe94398f60b364160cb78fd2a7b1f400b53e8437508" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

<h4>use</h4>
<p>The function <code>Com_TxConfirmation</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00124" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00124">[SWS_Com_00124]</a>) serves to confirm to the COM module, by lower layer communication interface modules (Lower Layer Communication Interface), the successful transmission or the failure of the transmission of a PDU.</p>
<p>The call is synchronous (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00124" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00124">[SWS_Com_00124]</a>). The function has no return value (<code>void</code>) and no input/output or output parameters (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00124" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00124">[SWS_Com_00124]</a>). Passing is performed via two input parameters (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00124" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00124">[SWS_Com_00124]</a>):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>TxPduId</code> (type <code>PduIdType</code>): Identifier of the PDU that was transmitted (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00124" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00124">[SWS_Com_00124]</a>).</li>
<li><code>result</code> (type <code>Std_ReturnType</code>): Confirmation status of the transmission. The value <code>E_OK</code> signals the successful transmission of the PDU, while <code>E_NOT_OK</code> indicates a failure of the transmission (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00124" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00124">[SWS_Com_00124]</a>).</li>
</ul>
<h4>Concurrency and Integration</h4>
<p>With regard to concurrency, <code>Com_TxConfirmation</code> is reentrant for different PDU IDs, but non-reentrant for the same PDU ID (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00124" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00124">[SWS_Com_00124]</a>).</p>
<p>The interface is specified under the service ID <code>0x40</code> and is provided via the header <code>Com.h</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00124" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00124">[SWS_Com_00124]</a>).</p>
<p class="ai-note">This usage note was created automatically based on the specification of the module Com in AUTOSAR Classic Release R20-11.</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="bdd9e9ad80ba22b158b82da8614d82f478ff67d04615c381338bff3fd51adfbe" data-trace-output="a1c10ca9cacf6a1d510328e595fbebfba285cf36795eac386a5be1df93eff08d" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>Usage and Semantics</h4>
  <p>The function <code>Com_SendSignal</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00197" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00197">[SWS_Com_00197]</a>) is used to update a signal object identified by parameter <code>SignalId</code> with the data pointed to by pointer <code>SignalDataPtr</code>. The function call operates asynchronously and is provided via the header file <code>Com.h</code>.</p>
  <h4>Error Handling and Return Values</h4>
  <p>The service returns a status value of type <code>uint8</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00197" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00197">[SWS_Com_00197]</a>):</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The request was successfully accepted by the service.</li>
    <li><code>COM_SERVICE_NOT_AVAILABLE</code>: The associated I-PDU group is stopped, or execution failed due to a development error.</li>
    <li><code>COM_BUSY</code>: The TP buffer is currently locked for handling large data types.</li>
  </ul>
  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>Regarding reentrancy, <code>Com_SendSignal</code> is reentrant for different signals, but explicitly non-reentrant for the same signal (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00197" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00197">[SWS_Com_00197]</a>).</p>
  <h4>Interaction</h4>
  <p>If the parameter <code>ComSignalGroupArrayAccess</code> is defined for a signal group, calling <code>Com_SendSignal</code> for all group signals of that signal group is not supported (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00843" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00843">[SWS_Com_00843]</a>).</p>
  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification of AUTOSAR Classic Release R20-11.</p>
</div>

  <h4>Usage and Semantics</h4>
  <p>The synchronous function <code>Com_ReceiveSignal</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00198" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00198">[SWS_Com_00198]</a>) copies the data of the signal identified via parameter <code>SignalId</code> to the destination address specified via pointer <code>SignalDataPtr</code>.</p>

  <h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
  <p>The return value of type <code>uint8</code> reports the status of the function execution (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00198" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00198">[SWS_Com_00198]</a>):</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The service was successfully accepted and executed.</li>
    <li><code>COM_SERVICE_NOT_AVAILABLE</code>: The associated I-PDU group was stopped, or the service failed as a result of a development error.</li>
    <li><code>COM_BUSY</code>: The TP buffer is locked for handling large data types.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00198" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00198">[SWS_Com_00198]</a>, the function is reentrant for different signals, but non-reentrant for the same signal.</p>

  <h4>Interaction and Configuration</h4>
  <p>If the parameter <code>ComSignalGroupArrayAccess</code> (<code>ECUC_Com_10003</code>) is defined for a signal group, calling <code>Com_ReceiveSignal</code> for group signals of this signal group is not supported (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00843" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00843">[SWS_Com_00843]</a>).</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification AUTOSAR CP R20-11.</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="7f55e37045f5edbfe33cd90ca809093f5b69e5f4635098e0fd60447de7dc8b0c" data-trace-output="be1999c4bf4c5e71553a35b090a83f69cf00d23aaf07b53c2c7b4e300bcb5fdd" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>use</h4>
  <p>The function <code>Com_SendSignalGroup</code> copies the contents of the assigned shadow buffer into the associated I-PDU (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00200" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00200">[SWS_Com_00200]</a>). Transmission is performed asynchronously (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00200" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00200">[SWS_Com_00200]</a>). The identifier of the signal group to be sent is specified via the input parameter <code>SignalGroupId</code> of type <code>Com_SignalGroupIdType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00200" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00200">[SWS_Com_00200]</a>).</p>

  <h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
  <p>The return value of type <code>uint8</code> provides information about the status of the function execution (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00200" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00200">[SWS_Com_00200]</a>):</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The service request was successfully accepted (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00200" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00200">[SWS_Com_00200]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>COM_SERVICE_NOT_AVAILABLE</code>: The corresponding I-PDU group was stopped or the service call failed due to a development error (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00200" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00200">[SWS_Com_00200]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>COM_BUSY</code>: The TP buffer is locked for handling large data types (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00200" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00200">[SWS_Com_00200]</a>).</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>The function is non-reentrant for the same signal group, but reentrant for different signal groups (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00200" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00200">[SWS_Com_00200]</a>). If <code>ComSignalGroupArrayAccess</code> is configured for a signal group, calling <code>Com_SendSignalGroup</code> is not supported for this signal group (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00843" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00843">[SWS_Com_00843]</a>).</p>

  <h4>Interaction</h4>
  <p>The AUTOSAR COM module treats a call to <code>Com_SendSignalGroupArray</code> equivalently to <code>Com_SendSignalGroup</code> with respect to the transmission properties of signal groups, the selection of the I-PDU transmission mode, and signal routing (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00847" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00847">[SWS_Com_00847]</a>).</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR R20-11 specification.</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="3186abdbb8bcf81cc82eacd7fb76308587860113280c9ae17b40852ae0563933" data-trace-output="2bcacf232178317c740818bb55df965053481aedb38c65ac447ded3769daf6f0" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

<h4>use</h4>
<p>The synchronous function <code>Com_ReceiveSignalGroup</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00201" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00201">[SWS_Com_00201]</a>) copies a received signal group from the I-PDU into the assigned shadow buffer. The signal group to be read is specified via the input parameter <code>SignalGroupId</code> of type <code>Com_SignalGroupIdType</code>.</p>
<h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
<p>The return value of type <code>uint8</code> signals the result of the execution (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00201" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00201">[SWS_Com_00201]</a>):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>E_OK</code>: The service call was successfully accepted.</li>
<li><code>COM_SERVICE_NOT_AVAILABLE</code>: The associated I-PDU group was stopped or the service failed due to a development error.</li>
<li><code>COM_BUSY</code>: The TP buffer is locked for processing large data types.</li>
</ul>
<h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
<p>Regarding concurrency, <code>Com_ReceiveSignalGroup</code> is reentrant for different signal groups, but non-reentrant for the same signal group (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00201" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00201">[SWS_Com_00201]</a>).</p>
<h4>Interaction</h4>
<p>If <code>ComSignalGroupArrayAccess</code> is configured for a signal group, calling <code>Com_ReceiveSignalGroup</code> for this group is not supported (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00843" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00843">[SWS_Com_00843]</a>). Likewise, in this case, calling <code>Com_ReceiveSignal</code> for the associated group signals is not permissible (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00843" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00843">[SWS_Com_00843]</a>).</p>
<p class="ai-note">This usage note is based on the specifications of release R20-11.</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="33eecb47754fda37031442c12d165556be5321939ba0887ebd869db1cb19eddf" data-trace-output="951568f5b3d9920909d9a1469fe930727fab6a78bada7cfadc9cd1809510817c" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>Usage and Semantics</h4>
  <p>
    The function <code>Com_InvalidateSignal</code> invalidates a signal by setting its value to the configured value <code>ComSignalDataInvalidValue</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00203" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00203">[SWS_Com_00203]</a>). The call is provided via the header <code>Com.h</code> and operates asynchronously (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00203" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00203">[SWS_Com_00203]</a>).
  </p>
  <p>
    As an input parameter, the function expects <code>SignalId</code> of type <code>Com_SignalIdType</code>, which specifies the identifier of the signal to be invalidated (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00203" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00203">[SWS_Com_00203]</a>).
  </p>

  <h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
  <p>
    The service returns a status value of type <code>uint8</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00203" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00203">[SWS_Com_00203]</a>):
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The request for signal invalidation was successfully accepted (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00203" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00203">[SWS_Com_00203]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>COM_SERVICE_NOT_AVAILABLE</code>: The service is not available. This occurs if the associated I-PDU group is stopped, no <code>ComSignalDataInvalidValue</code> was configured for the specified <code>SignalId</code>, or the call fails due to a development error (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00203" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00203">[SWS_Com_00203]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>COM_BUSY</code>: The buffer of the transport protocol (TP buffer) is currently locked (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00203" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00203">[SWS_Com_00203]</a>).</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Reentrancy</h4>
  <p>
    Regarding reentrancy, <code>Com_InvalidateSignal</code> is non-reentrant for the same signal, but reentrant for different signals (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00203" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00203">[SWS_Com_00203]</a>). Callers must therefore ensure that concurrent invalidation calls for the same signal ID are avoided or synchronized.
  </p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification of AUTOSAR CP R20-11.</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="8a216e409b6281519172cabc5dd7b37648a43b5fb8a762ae1c3a2f495dcb43eb" data-trace-output="0ae1e35f49a845d9d18f26ef4d7f7a13806e92b09ceb2134502785b268817fdc" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>use</h4>
  <p>The configurable callout function <code>Com_TxIpduCallout</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00346" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00346">[SWS_Com_00346]</a>) is called on the sender side to perform user-defined transmission filtering (<em>user-defined transmission filtering</em>) or user-defined pre-transmission processing (<em>user-defined pre-transmission-processing</em>) before transmitting an outgoing I-PDU.</p>
  <p>The call is synchronous (<em>Synchronous</em>) under service ID <code>0x29</code>. For reentrancy, <em>don't care</em> is specified.</p>

  <h4>Parameters and Return Value</h4>
  <ul>
    <li><code>PduId</code> (in): Designates the identifier of the transmitted I-PDU (<em>ID of the transmitted I-PDU</em>).</li>
    <li><code>PduInfoPtr</code> (inout): Pointer to structure <code>PduInfoType</code>. It contains the length (<code>SduLength</code>) of the sent I-PDU as well as a pointer to its payload data (<code>SduDataPtr</code>).</li>
  </ul>
  <p>Via the boolean return value, the callout decides on the further course of action:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>true</code>: The I-PDU is processed further normally (<em>I-PDU will be processed normal</em>).</li>
    <li><code>false</code>: The I-PDU is discarded and not processed further (<em>I-PDU will not be processed any further</em>).</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Error Handling and Concurrency</h4>
  <p>No DET or DEM error messages are defined in the specification element for <code>Com_TxIpduCallout</code>. Since reentrancy is declared as <em>don't care</em>, the specification places no specific requirements on the reentrancy of the implementation.</p>

  <p class="ai-note">Created based on specification <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00346" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00346">[SWS_Com_00346]</a> from AUTOSAR CP R20-11.</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="161a524cbd436e168477fb43d682205cd5bfd6ec29de6a6e09cb5b4989808ddc" data-trace-output="9f8fae5fd68b932afabb8382514e4c3abcd103fbc3360c0c31721a1fc9f9713b" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>use</h4>
  <p>The synchronous function <code>Com_TriggerIPDUSend</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00348" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00348">[SWS_Com_00348]</a>) is used for the targeted triggering of the transmission of an I-PDU based on the input parameter <code>PduId</code>. The interface is provided via the header <code>Com.h</code>.</p>
  
  <h4>Error Handling and Return Values</h4>
  <p>The function returns as return value of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00348" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00348">[SWS_Com_00348]</a>):</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: Transmission of the I-PDU was successfully initiated.</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The I-PDU is in the stopped state; transmission could not be initiated.</li>
  </ul>
  <p>According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00861" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00861">[SWS_Com_00861]</a>, AUTOSAR COM initiates the transmission of the affected I-PDU only if the I-PDU is started.</p>

  <h4>Interaction with Large I-PDUs</h4>
  <p>If a large I-PDU (Large I-PDU) is triggered via <code>Com_TriggerIPDUSend</code> and its buffer is currently locked, AUTOSAR COM does not discard the transmit request. Instead, the transmit request is buffered and the I-PDU is automatically transmitted as soon as the buffer is released again (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00867" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00867">[SWS_Com_00867]</a>).</p>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>The function is specified as non-reentrant (<code>Non Reentrant</code>) (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00348" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00348">[SWS_Com_00348]</a>). Therefore, calls with identical contexts must not occur concurrently or preemptively without appropriate synchronization.</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated based on the AUTOSAR specification R20-11.</p>
</div>

  <h4>use</h4>
  <p>The function <code>Com_InvalidateSignalGroup</code> invalidates all group signals of the signal group identified via the input parameter <code>SignalGroupId</code> (of type <code>Com_SignalGroupIdType</code>) by setting their values to the respective configured invalidity values (<code>Com Signal Data Invalid Values</code>) <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00557" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00557">[SWS_Com_00557]</a>. The interface is provided via <code>Com.h</code>, has the service ID <code>0x1b</code>, and is specified as asynchronous <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00557" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00557">[SWS_Com_00557]</a>.</p>

  <h4>Error Handling and Return Values</h4>
  <p>The return value of type <code>uint8</code> provides information about the acceptance or the error cause of the operation <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00557" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00557">[SWS_Com_00557]</a>:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The service call was successfully accepted <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00557" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00557">[SWS_Com_00557]</a>.</li>
    <li><code>COM_BUSY</code>: Processing cannot take place if the transport protocol buffer (TP buffer) is locked <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00557" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00557">[SWS_Com_00557]</a>.</li>
    <li><code>COM_SERVICE_NOT_AVAILABLE</code>: The service is not available; this is the case if the associated I-PDU group is stopped, no invalidity value (<code>Com Signal Data Invalid Value</code>) is configured for any of the group signals, or the call fails due to a development error <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00557" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00557">[SWS_Com_00557]</a>.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>With respect to concurrent access, <code>Com_InvalidateSignalGroup</code> is defined as non-reentrant for the same signal group, but reentrant for different signal groups <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00557" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00557">[SWS_Com_00557]</a>.</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note is based on the AUTOSAR CP R20-11 specification.</p>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="1c35e48ab9505d987f003e869adc87af5adcbc98e66ad6ca68c3dee023973a61" data-trace-output="659683e7c1fbe2d22d2bee61ba8af68c313223302aa55c31788a2d9c507d1576" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

<h4>Usage and Semantics</h4>
<p>The function <code>Com_SendDynSignal</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00627" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00627">[SWS_Com_00627]</a>) is used to update a dynamic length signal. The target signal is addressed via the parameter <code>SignalId</code>, <code>SignalDataPtr</code> points to the payload data to be transmitted, and <code>Length</code> specifies the length of the dynamic signal. The service operates asynchronously and updates the signal object identified by <code>SignalId</code>.</p>

<h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
<p>The return value of type <code>uint8</code> indicates the result of the call:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>E_OK</code>: The service call was successfully accepted.</li>
<li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The passed <code>Length</code> exceeds the configured maximum length <code>ComSignalLength</code> of the signal.</li>
<li><code>COM_SERVICE_NOT_AVAILABLE</code>: The associated I-PDU group is stopped or the service failed due to a development error.</li>
<li><code>COM_BUSY</code>: The TP buffer is currently locked.</li>
</ul>

<h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
<p>According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00627" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00627">[SWS_Com_00627]</a>, the function is reentrant for different signals (<em>Reentrant for different signals</em>), but non-reentrant for the same signal (<em>Non Reentrant for the same signal</em>). Callers must therefore ensure that parallel calls for the same <code>SignalId</code> are avoided or synchronized.</p>

<p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR specification R20-11.</p>
</div>

  <h4>Usage and Call Context</h4>
  <p>
    The function <code>Com_TpRxIndication</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00650" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00650">[SWS_Com_00650]</a>) is called after the reception of an I-PDU via the TP API. The parameter <code>result</code> signals to the AUTOSAR COM module whether the preceding reception process was successfully completed or failed. The interface is provided via the header <code>Com.h</code> and has the service ID <code>0x45</code>.
  </p>
  <p>
    The call is synchronous and the function is specified as reentrant. It has no return value (return type <code>void</code>).
  </p>

  <h4>Parameters</h4>
  <ul>
    <li>
      <code>id</code> (<code>PduIdType</code>, In): Identification of the received I-PDU.
    </li>
    <li>
      <code>result</code> (<code>Std_ReturnType</code>, In): Result of the reception process.
    </li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Error Handling and Interaction</h4>
  <p>
    If <code>Com_TpRxIndication</code> is called with the value <code>E_NOT_OK</code> for the parameter <code>result</code>, the error behavior defined in <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00838" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00838">[SWS_Com_00838]</a> takes effect: In this case, the AUTOSAR COM module treats all signals of the received large I-PDU like invalidated signals. Consequently, the module executes the respectively configured <code>ComDataInvalidActions</code> for all signals and signal groups contained in the I-PDU.
  </p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR specification R20-11.</p>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="eba52a8227fcde2b9a50ecb85fa0f1c23b5de0114e9f8cfdd52c42fd4467f391" data-trace-output="16a1a5600eb387b77673f1d3f930b63d2b22ba9bbdc4c088338553bef447b4d7" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>Usage and Semantics</h4>
  <p>
    The function <code>Com_ReceiveDynSignal</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00690" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00690">[SWS_Com_00690]</a>) represents a synchronous service that copies payload data of a signal with dynamic length. The desired signal is addressed via parameter <code>SignalId</code>. The received data is copied to the memory location pointed to by <code>SignalDataPtr</code>, while the actual signal length is returned via <code>Length</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00690" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00690">[SWS_Com_00690]</a>).
  </p>
  <p>
    The parameter <code>Length</code> functions as an in/out parameter: Upon the call, it must specify the maximum receivable buffer size as input. After successful processing, it contains the actual length of the received dynamic signal as output (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00690" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00690">[SWS_Com_00690]</a>). The interface is available via header <code>Com.h</code>.
  </p>

  <h4>Error Handling and Return Values</h4>
  <p>
    The execution status is signaled via the return value of type <code>uint8</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00690" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00690">[SWS_Com_00690]</a>):
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The service was successfully accepted and the data was copied.</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The value of <code>Length</code> passed as input is smaller than the actual length of the received dynamic signal.</li>
    <li><code>COM_SERVICE_NOT_AVAILABLE</code>: The associated I-PDU group was stopped or the service failed due to a development error.</li>
    <li><code>COM_BUSY</code>: The associated transport protocol buffer (TP buffer) is locked.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>
    <code>Com_ReceiveDynSignal</code> is reentrant for different signals, but not reentrant for the same signal (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00690" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00690">[SWS_Com_00690]</a>). Concurrent calls for the same <code>SignalId</code> must therefore be avoided by appropriate protection mechanisms at the caller level.
  </p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification of AUTOSAR Classic Release R20-11.</p>
</div>

  <p>
    The synchronous and reentrant function <code>Com_StartReception</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00691" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00691">[SWS_Com_00691]</a>) is called at the start of the reception of an N-SDU. This comprises both segmented transmissions (First Frame with subsequent Consecutive Frames) and unsegmented individual frames (Single Frame). The declaration is available via <code>Com.h</code>.
  </p>
  <h4>Parameters and Call Semantics</h4>
  <ul>
    <li><code>id</code>: Identification of the I-PDU to be received.</li>
    <li><code>info</code>: Pointer to an <code>PduInfoType</code> structure containing payload data as well as metadata of the first or individual frame. If neither payload nor metadata is present, this parameter must be set to <code>NULL_PTR</code>.</li>
    <li><code>TpSduLength</code>: Total length of the N-SDU to be received. If the service is called with an <code>TpSduLength</code> of 0, it returns the currently maximum available buffer size.</li>
    <li><code>bufferSizePtr</code>: Output parameter for the buffer available in the receiving module. This value serves the calling transport protocol module for calculating the Block Size (BS).</li>
  </ul>
  <h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
  <p>
    The result of the buffer request is signaled via the return type <code>BufReq_ReturnType</code>:
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>BUFREQ_OK</code>: The connection is accepted and reception continues. <code>bufferSizePtr</code> contains the size of the available buffer. If no buffer of the requested size can be provided, the value 0 is returned via <code>bufferSizePtr</code>.</li>
    <li><code>BUFREQ_E_NOT_OK</code>: The connection is rejected and the reception process is aborted. The value of <code>bufferSizePtr</code> remains unchanged.</li>
    <li><code>BUFREQ_E_OVFL</code>: No buffer of the required length can be allocated; reception aborts and <code>bufferSizePtr</code> remains unchanged.</li>
  </ul>
  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated by an AI based on the specification state of AUTOSAR CP R20-11.</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="516aabd6462f98c433110f165c5584501c85ca1cda36b06d848de721479aa0d1" data-trace-output="795ff28f0ea8808d97ab0f41971f795540a4557c087cd0943d49698ccd3cff26" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>use</h4>
  <p>The synchronous interface <code>Com_CopyTxData</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00693" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00693">[SWS_Com_00693]</a>) is called by lower-layer modules (such as transport protocols) to query transmit data for segments (N-PDUs) of an I-PDU. Each call sequentially provides the next data segment, provided no retransmission is requested.</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>id</code>: Identifies the I-PDU to be transmitted.</li>
    <li><code>info</code>: Points to the buffer structure (<code>PduInfoType</code>). <code>SduDataPtr</code> receives the data, <code>SduLength</code> determines the requested byte count. A value of <code>0</code> for <code>SduLength</code> can be used to signal state changes via <code>retry</code> or to query remaining data; in this case, <code>SduDataPtr</code> may be a <code>NULL_PTR</code>.</li>
    <li><code>retry</code>: Controls confirmation and error recovery. If the pointer is <code>NULL_PTR</code>, copied data may be removed from the buffer immediately after copying. If it points to a structure (<code>RetryInfoType</code>), <code>TpDataState</code> determines the behavior:
      <ul>
        <li><code>TP_CONFPENDING</code>: Previously copied data must remain in the TP buffer for error recovery.</li>
        <li><code>TP_DATACONF</code>: Confirms all data copied prior to this call so that it may be deleted (excluding data of the current call).</li>
        <li><code>TP_DATARETRY</code>: Instructs the function to copy data again starting from the offset <code>TxTpDataCnt</code> (relative to the current copy position).</li>
      </ul>
    </li>
    <li><code>availableDataPtr</code>: Writes the number of bytes remaining in the Tx buffer as an output parameter, which enables TP modules with dynamic payload length to determine the size of subsequent segments.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
  <p>The result of the request is reported via <code>BufReq_ReturnType</code>:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>BUFREQ_OK</code>: Data was completely copied into the buffer as requested.</li>
    <li><code>BUFREQ_E_BUSY</code>: Data could not be provided because the required amount is not yet available in the upper module. No data was copied; the lower-layer module may repeat the call later.</li>
    <li><code>BUFREQ_E_NOT_OK</code>: The request failed; no data was copied.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency</h4>
  <p>According to the specification, the function is defined as reentrant (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00693" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00693">[SWS_Com_00693]</a>).</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note is based on the AUTOSAR CP R20-11 specification.</p>
</div>

  <h4>Usage and Semantics</h4>
  <p>
    The call to <code>Com_RxIpduCallout</code> is performed synchronously with service ID <code>0x2A</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00700" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00700">[SWS_Com_00700]</a>). The function has two input parameters:

    <li><code>PduInfoPtr</code>: Pointer to a structure of type <code>PduInfoType</code>, which provides the length (<code>SduLength</code>) of the received I-PDU as well as a pointer to its payload (<code>SduDataPtr</code>) (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00700" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00700">[SWS_Com_00700]</a>).</li>

  </p>
  <h4>Return Values and Filtering</h4>
  <p>
    Via the return value of type <code>boolean</code>, the processing flow in the COM module is controlled (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00700" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00700">[SWS_Com_00700]</a>):
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>true</code>: The received I-PDU is processed normally.</li>
    <li><code>false</code>: The I-PDU is discarded and not processed further.</li>
  </ul>
  <h4>Concurrency and Error Handling</h4>
  <p>
    Regarding reentrancy, the function is classified with the property <em>don't care</em> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00700" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00700">[SWS_Com_00700]</a>).   <h4>Usage and Call Context</h4>
  <p>The callback function <code>Com_CbkCounterErr</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00726" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00726">[SWS_Com_00726]</a>) serves to signal incorrect I-PDU counter values. It is called immediately by the AUTOSAR COM module as soon as an incoming I-PDU has a counter value that deviates from the expected value.</p>
  <p>The call is performed synchronously (<em>Synchronous</em>) and returns no value (<code>void</code>). The following context information is transmitted via the input parameters:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>ComPduId</code> (<code>PduIdType</code>): The identifier of the I-PDU in which the counter error was detected.</li>
    <li><code>ExpectedCounter</code> (<code>uint8</code>): The counter value expected by the COM module.</li>
    <li><code>ReceivedCounter</code> (<code>uint8</code>): The counter value transmitted in the received I-PDU.</li>
  </ul>
  <h4>Concurrency and Error Handling</h4>
  <p>For reentrancy, <em>don't care</em> is specified (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00726" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00726">[SWS_Com_00726]</a>). Since the function is called immediately upon detection of the deviation, the actual execution context (e.g. task or interrupt context) is likely to depend on the configuration of the higher-level reception processing.</p>
  <p>The provision of the callback interface is configurable (<em>Available via configurable</em>). Specific error codes, standardized DET/DEM messages, or return values for error handling are not defined in <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Com_00726" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Com_00726">[SWS_Com_00726]</a>.</p>
